question_MULTILINES: The attached video is a single programme from a very diverse collection at a national screen archive.
Sometimes a professional programme can contain raw unedited rushes with outtakes or retakes.
Returns a json dictionary with the following keys:
* year (the year the programme was made, only if specified and certain),
* title (the title of the programme, only if specified and certain),
* places (unique toponyms where the programme takes place; only if certain and mentioned on a sign or in subtitles),
* segments (list of main chapters or major segments, for each a `title` and a `starting` timecode),
* summary (one very concise sentence summarising the content of the programme),
* synopsis (short paragraph summarising the content of the programme; don't mention possible visual transitions at the start),
* colour (either: black-and-white or colour or sepia or colour-and-black-and-white),

* category (one or more values from: Travel and transportation; Home and family; Sport and leisure; Landscape and buildings; Industry and occupations; Wartime; Culture and traditions; Health, Welfare and Education; No idea),

* category2 (one or more values from: Cinema Newsreel; Local Cinema Topicals; Promotional/Advertising; Educational/Training; Scientific; Factual Record; Fiction; Home Movies; Special Interest; Amateur),
* keywords (10 key topical or thematic tags for this programme; avoid overly specific tags like place names, people or objects),
* credits (if specified; use a dictionary with keys for roles and name(s) for values).

sep1.question: List every full-screen separator between distinct programmes. A visual separator usually looks like SMPTE color bars, blank screen, production card, countdown leaders, static or white noise. It is always totally distinct in style from surrounding programmes, usually non-photographic and never intended for public audience. Compare with programmes on either side of the separator to confirm this. Return an empty list if the input doesn't contain any definite separator. Other screens within a programme like ending credits or chapter titles should not be reported as programme separators but may help finding/confirming nearby separators.
